Consult Summary:
- 27-year-old male with immediate localized reaction after a bee/wasp sting to the arm and anxiety with subjective dyspnea and oral sensations; video exam shows no objective airway compromise. Managed conservatively with antihistamines and strict return precautions for anaphylaxis.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Difficulty breathing after recent bee/wasp sting; localized rash at sting site; sensation of mild right-sided lip swelling; tongue feels “weird.”
- Onset/duration: Sting occurred minutes before the consult.
- Course/severity: Patient does not feel acutely breathless now; sought reassurance due to concern it might worsen.
- Location: Sting on arm with mild redness and puncture mark noted.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: No medications taken yet; no treatments tried prior to call.
- Associated symptoms: Anxiety; concern about possible lip/tongue swelling.
- Pertinent negatives (from encounter): No visible lip swelling to clinician; breathing and speech appeared normal to clinician during video review.

Past Medical History:
- Eczema (atopy).
- Anxiety/panic attacks (occasional; no medications).
- No history of anaphylaxis.
- No prior epinephrine autoinjector.

Medications:
- Current: None reported for this episode.
- Allergies: Penicillin (reaction details not documented).

Social History:
- Occupation: Computer scientist.
- Living situation: Lives alone.
- Pets: Has a cat; no known pet allergies.
- Tobacco/alcohol/substance use: Not recorded.

Family History:
- No known family history of acute allergic reactions or other relevant illnesses noted.

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not recorded.
- General/Respiratory (video): Breathing appeared normal; speaking comfortably; no audible stridor or wheeze.
- Oropharynx/lips (video): No visible lip swelling; oropharyngeal view unremarkable.
- Skin (sting site): Localized slight redness/blotchiness with puncture mark on arm; no notable swelling observed by clinician.
- Other systems: Not recorded.

Investigations:
- None ordered; no results available.

Assessment & Plan:
- Overall Impression:
  - Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to Hymenoptera sting (bee/wasp) with anxiety-related symptoms; no current objective evidence of anaphylaxis or airway compromise.

- DDx Integration (brief):
  - Localized allergic/inflammatory reaction to sting (high likelihood): Immediate local erythema and puncture mark; normal breathing and oropharyngeal exam. Opposes: subjective lip/tongue sensations.
  - Early anaphylaxis (medium concern): Temporal association with sting and subjective dyspnea/oral sensations. Opposes: no visible swelling, stable exam, no progression or systemic features reported.
  - Anxiety-related dyspnea (medium): History of anxiety; normal observed respirations. Opposes: occurred immediately after sting, which could also indicate allergic reaction.

- Issue 1: Hymenoptera sting—localized reaction
  - Plan:
    - Start an antihistamine:
      - Chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg, up to six times daily (as advised). Route/frequency beyond this not documented.
      - Alternatively, a once-daily antihistamine (specific agent/dose not documented).
    - Monitor the sting area; if redness spreads, area becomes hot, or signs of local infection develop, contact the clinic as antibiotics may be needed.

- Issue 2: Anaphylaxis risk education/safety netting
  - Plan:
    - Urgent Emergency Department (ED) evaluation if any new or worsening red flags: swelling of lips/tongue, difficulty breathing, noisy/rasping breathing (stridor), voice change, or rapidly progressing symptoms.
    - If concerned or if symptoms evolve but are not severe, contact the practice promptly for reassessment.
    - An information link on anaphylaxis warning signs was provided by the clinician.

- Issue 3: Anxiety/panic symptoms
  - Plan:
    - Reassurance provided; advised low threshold to contact the practice if anxiety escalates or for further guidance.

- General plan items:
  - No allergy testing indicated at present; consider if reactions become recurrent or non-specific rashes occur (per clinician discussion).
  - No epinephrine autoinjector prescribed at this time.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vital signs not recorded; comprehensive medication list and doses not reviewed; details of penicillin reaction not specified.
- Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx; both support localized reaction with safety-netting for potential early anaphylaxis.
- Transcript quality: Clear; video exam performed with adequate visualization of lips/oropharynx.
